proposition.claim:
Explicit nonlinear family formulas sum per-coordinate kernels, whereas intended joint construction permits interactions

Thresholding should yield an acyclic graph before cooldown

Discrete comparison estimates error only due to posterior overlap and supports the low-error cost of flexible multivariate Bayesian discovery. The paper also states an expectation of higher error due to continuous-relaxation optimization; this tentative comparison is not treated as a failed universal claim. The Major finding is anchored to the explicit overlap-only isolation.

repair.content:
Specify joint scaled Euclidean distance separately for each nonlinear kernel family; retain sum across families

Use exact acyclicity of binary support and delete an edge while cyclic

Describe the discrete and continuous results as complete approximate-procedure performance and remove the overlap-only isolation interpretation. Preserve the tentative expectation of higher error from continuous-relaxation optimization without asserting that the comparison quantifies or isolates that contribution.
